fixture_name: M5 Junction 10 Improvements — UK Stage 1 (real scheme, OGL)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Checking refuge dimension/capacity against bus-stop-generated crossing demand on wide A4019 arms is a genuine Stage 1 preliminary-design safety issue with a credible injury mechanism.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal refuge-width/clipping hazard is directly supported by the verbatim EV-UK-015 quote; the bus-stop demand element rests on the cited Stage 1 decision-log assumption rather than a second evidence_id.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a GG 119 safety concern rather than a compliance question, with no conflation of framework categories and appropriate null normative_basis_note.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific and actionable—names the design users (expectant parent with pushchair plus cycle), the elements (refuge depth and width), and each affected crossing point—at a viable detailed-design stage.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians and cyclists are explicitly identified, with pushchair and cycle accommodation addressed in both the scenario and the recommendation.

justifications.substance: Verifying that assessed refuse-vehicle and 7.5t box-van envelopes (which already show limited over-run into opposing lanes) remain valid after stop-line repositioning is a genuine geometric-safety/compliance issue at this junction.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal basis is grounded: EV-UK-002 verbatim quote confirms the existing swept-path assessment and its over-run caveat, and the stop-line repositioning is presented as a recorded input fact rather than invented content.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a compliance_question with an explicit exception-check analog note, keeping the confirmatory check categorically distinct from any asserted safety problem and explicitly not asserting VRU exposure.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific and actionable: re-run large-vehicle swept-path analysis over the as-adjusted stop-line positions, with a clear Stage 2 deadline; not a null recommendation.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians and cyclists, central refuges, and recorded desire lines are acknowledged as relevant context, but no VRU-specific impact is analysed within the finding, consistent with an acknowledged-but-scoped-out treatment.
